qt: to the Commission Kostas Papadakis (NI), Lefteris Nikolaou-Alavanos (NI) Subject:

The report which DG AGRI recently addressed to the Greek Government and authorities reveals chaotic and systemic shortcomings in the management of EAGF and EAFRD payments for the period 2023-2026. Meanwhile, payments have been decoupled from actual production, certification has been turned into a business, staff cuts have left state inspection services completely understaffed and physical on-the-spot checks have been replaced by bureaucratic/remote methods. In addition, the responsibilities of the OPEKEPE paying agency have now been transferred to the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE), which has done nothing to address the crux of the issue or the causes of the scandals. In light of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What view does it take of the fact that the CAP institutional framework itself, by decoupling aid from production, privatising checks/certifications, leaving public services understaffed and shifting responsibilities, once again to the detriment of struggling producers, creates a breeding ground for scandal, while at the same time threatening cuts that will once again affect the same people?
What is the exact level of flat-rate corrections and what funding amounts is it considering withholding from Greece for the period 2023-2026?

How does it assess the apparent total failure of the transfer of OPEKEPE’s responsibilities to the AADE, which confirms farmers’ complaints that it was done with a view to collecting taxes and seizing aid due to outstanding debts, rather than ensuring timely payments to real producers?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.11.2026) The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) is implemented in shared management where the Commission reimburses expenditure to Member States, who pay the farmers. The management and control framework for the CAP is made up of different public authorities, but it is not privatised. It is for Member States to adequately staff and equip these authorities, while the Commission audits the functioning of the system. The CAP functions in a marketbased system, where farmers receive support for performing certain actions, not based on the produced volumes. In the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) 2028-2034 the CAP is integrated into the National and Regional Partnership (NRP) Fund. The proposal for the future CAP after 2028 offers largely the same interventions as today. Greece has taken measures to improve the management of CAP funds, notably by transferring OPEKEPE to the Independent Authority of Public Revenue (AADE), as part of an Action Plan to address audit findings. On 12 March 2026, Greece informed the Commission that it had reinstated the accreditation of the paying agency and incorporated it into AADE. In case of serious deficiencies in the Member States' management and control systems, the Commission applies financial corrections to protect the Union’s budget. Audits for the CAP 2023-2027 period are still ongoing. Any financial correction1,2 will be determined based on the nature, duration and gravity of the deficiencies identified, as well as the risk posed to the EU budget. Under the shared management of the CAP, Member States should ensure that payments are disbursed to the beneficiaries in full and within the payment deadlines laid down by EU law3 after sufficient checks have been carried out by the national authorities to ensure the funds reach genuine farmers. It is the responsibility of the Member State to ensure that the management and control systems function properly and to address any shortcomings. CAP funds should be spent protecting the EU budget and in line with principles of sound financial management.
1 Article 55 of the Regulation (EU) No 2021/2116 - https://eur-

lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/2116/oj/eng?uri=CELEX:32021R2116. 2 Communication from the Commission – Guidelines on the calculation of the financial corrections in the framework of the conformity and financial clearance of accounts procedures C/2024/5991 - https://eurlex.europa.eu/eli/C/2024/5991/oj/eng. 3 Article 38, Article 44 and Article 59 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2116.
